videos.title: Your path in the Academy in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Your path in the MoRo Academy. Seven levels, from awareness to master instructor. L1 Awareness: anyone on the floor. L2 Operator, then L3A Technician or L3B Programmer. L4A Systems Engineer or L4B Advanced Programmer. L5 Master Instructor trains others. From L2 up, you also show it in practice.

videos.title: Meet MoRo in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Meet MoRo. MoRo is an autonomous mobile robot. It moves loads around your floor, on its own. No tape and no magnets on the floor. It maps the room with LiDAR, so it always knows where it is. Three models: A-250, A-500 and A-1200. Same navigation. Different payloads: 250, 500 and 1,200 kg. On screen at the end: Next: working safely around MoRo. MoRo Academy, DiFacto Robotics & Automation.

videos.title: Three models, three jobs in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Three models, three jobs. The A-250 carries up to 250 kg, and moves faster. It suits light assembly and small-item transport. The A-500 carries up to 500 kg. It is the most deployed, for machine tending. The A-1200 carries up to 1,200 kg, and moves slower. It suits heavy transfer and forklift replacement.

videos.title: Maps, not tape in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Maps, not tape. How MoRo finds its way. LiDAR measures distance with laser light. It sees walls, machines, pillars and people. SLAM locates MoRo and builds the map at once. So no floor tape or magnets are needed. Glass and mirror-like surfaces can confuse LiDAR. If the layout changes, the map needs updating.

videos.title: Meet the control interface in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: The control interface, in 30 seconds. MoRo is managed through software: the HMI. On MoRo, it is called ANT. You do not need a technical background. Most of the time, you supervise. You observe and confirm actions. You step in only when needed.

videos.title: The startup sequence in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: The startup sequence, in 30 seconds. First, a visual check: path clear, sensors unobstructed. Then power on: MoRo runs its own diagnostic. It checks battery, navigation and safety systems. Wait for the ready state. Only then assign a mission. Assigning early: a common cause of interrupted starts.

videos.title: Manual override and E-stop in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Manual override and E-stop, in 30 seconds. MoRo works autonomously by default. Override: setup repositioning, a blocked path, post-maintenance tests. Manual override does not disable safety systems. E-stop works the same in both modes. It takes immediate priority and halts all operation.

videos.title: The standards behind MoRo’s safety in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: The standards behind MoRo’s safety. MoRo’s safety is engineered to recognized standards. Not ad-hoc caution. ISO 3691-4: safety requirements for industrial trucks. ANSI B56.5: safety for guided industrial vehicles. You need not memorize them. Behavior around people follows requirements, not promises.

videos.title: If MoRo does something unexpected in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: If MoRo does something unexpected. It moves somewhere new, or stops for no clear reason. If there is any immediate concern, press E-stop. Then report it. Diagnosing is not the operator’s job at this level. Report early, even if it turns out minor.

videos.title: Working alongside MoRo in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Working alongside MoRo, in 30 seconds. Give MoRo room to finish its path. Do not assume its route stays the same each day. Move with clear, steady intent. Hesitating at its edge can make it slow or pause. Do not squeeze past it, or rest items on it. Treat it like any moving industrial equipment.

videos.title: A mission in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: A mission, in 30 seconds. A mission is one defined task. It has an origin, a destination and a finish condition. Before assigning, check MoRo is ready. And that the path is clear. Then supervise: steady and on time is normal. A stall or pause is your signal. Run any new mission once, under supervision. If it fails: note, assess, escalate if unclear.

videos.title: Five ways MoRo carries in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Five ways MoRo carries, in 30 seconds. MoRo supports five payload configurations. Conveyor, cobot interface and towing. Lifting, and lift-and-rotate. Each suits a different material handling need. The configuration changes what you check. Before a transfer, confirm the attachment is secure.

videos.title: The handshake in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: The handshake, in 30 seconds. When MoRo delivers to a machine, they must coordinate. Their exchange of signals is called a handshake. Signals confirm both sides are ready. Then that the handoff is complete. And they report any error state. If the exchange pauses and does not progress: stalled. Recognize a stalled handshake and flag it.

videos.title: Power and charging in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Power and charging, in 30 seconds. All MoRo models use LFP batteries. LFP is stable, long-lasting and fine with partial charges. MoRo is rated for 8 hours of runtime. The same on all three models. It charges wirelessly in under 1 hour. The charging dock must be placed and aligned correctly. On screen at the end: Next: placing and aligning the charging dock. MoRo Academy, DiFacto Robotics & Automation.

videos.title: Many robots, one floor in 30 seconds
videos.sectionTitle: From One Unit to a Fleet
videos.transcript: Many robots, one floor, in 30 seconds. More units move more material: throughput. Or keep work going if one is down: redundancy. Units see each other and avoid collisions automatically. Zones: shared paths and reserved routes. A deadlock is two units waiting on each other. The fleet system detects it and reroutes one unit.

videos.title: When something goes wrong in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: When something goes wrong, in 30 seconds. At L2 you recognize, categorize and escalate. You do not attempt the fix. Ask: what was MoRo doing just before? What does its status show now? Has anything changed around it? Share those details when you escalate.

videos.title: Conditions and loops in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Conditions and loops, in 30 seconds. A mission can include conditional logic. If a condition is met, take one path; otherwise, another. It can also repeat: a loop. A loop continues until a defined end state. One mission definition can cover more situations.

videos.title: Three kinds of maintenance in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Three kinds of maintenance, in 30 seconds. Preventive: scheduled work, whatever the condition. Predictive: triggered by signs of degradation. Corrective: fixing something after it has failed. A mature program relies on preventive and predictive. Corrective is the exception.

videos.title: Handling a battery safely in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Handling a battery safely. LFP is generally safer than many lithium chemistries. It still needs care. Lockout and tagout before any physical battery work. Watch for damage, unusual heat or swelling. Those go beyond routine replacement. Escalate immediately; do not keep handling.

videos.title: Symptom or root cause in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Symptom or root cause? A symptom: MoRo stops repeatedly in one area. A root cause: a sensor, a map or a mechanical issue. Treat only the symptom, and it comes back. First, confirm the symptom is reproducible. Then isolate which subsystem is implicated. Narrow it down with the fault tree and the interface.

videos.title: A good mapping pass in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: A good mapping pass, in 30 seconds. Map the space as it normally is. Typical equipment positions, no unusual obstructions. Guide MoRo through the space methodically. Cover every area it will need to navigate. Go at a deliberate pace, not a rushed one. LiDAR then builds an accurate picture as it goes.

videos.title: Do you need a zone in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Do you need a zone? In 30 seconds. Start with the facility’s real traffic patterns. Where is fleet density high? Where are passages too narrow for two units? Which routes are time-sensitive and need priority? Not every facility needs extensive zoning. Light traffic may need only minimal zones.

videos.title: Testing a handshake in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Testing a handshake, in 30 seconds. Signals must reach the right I/O points. A signal on the wrong point breaks the handshake. Even when both systems work fine. Test through many complete cycles, not just one. An intermittent failure points to timing or setup. One good test would have missed it.

videos.title: Commissioning a new site in 30 seconds
videos.sectionTitle: The Capstone of the Programmer Track
videos.transcript: Commissioning a new site, in 30 seconds. First, assess the site: layout, clearances, network. Then build the map, ideally in a quiet period. Program the core missions first, and keep them narrow. Validate each machine integration, again and again. Go-live is not the end: hand over to the operators. Document the map version, missions and integrations.

videos.title: Where MoRo plugs into the factory in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Where MoRo plugs into the factory. FANUC I/O: a request, ready, complete handshake. OPC-UA: data out to SCADA. MES and WMS APIs: orders in, reports out. A custom REST API: fleet control and third-party apps. Example: the MES sends a production order. MoRo does the move; status goes to SCADA.

videos.title: From production event to mission in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: From production event to mission. The MES records a production run as complete. That event can trigger a MoRo mission automatically. Or the WMS records a new order to fulfil. That can start a pick operation. No operator has to assign each mission by hand.

videos.title: How many robots in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: How many robots? In 30 seconds. Fleet size depends on three things. Throughput: how much moves, and how fast. Space: more units need more room. Redundancy: can the cell lose a unit? Oversize, and capital is wasted. Undersize, and throughput bottlenecks. Model real demand; do not guess.

videos.title: The machine tending cycle in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: The machine tending cycle, in 30 seconds. MoRo delivers raw material to the CNC machine. A handshake confirms the machine is ready. The CNC completes its machining operation. MoRo retrieves the finished part. Then it delivers the next raw material. The cycle repeats, so every handshake matters.
